The *Hetuhetusampayuttaduka, Kusalattika* is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna* collection [SuttaCentral]. Within the intricate combinatory framework of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the text treats the analytical intersection between the dyad of root causes and states associated with root causes (*hetu-hetusampayutta-duka*) and the triad of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states (*kusalattika*) [SuttaCentral].

No cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are identified for this text [DharmaNexus]. However, as is typical of the formulaic matrix structure of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the text displays extensive internal reuse across the Pali Abhidhamma corpus, sharing 116 matching passages with 21 other Pali texts according to DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus]. Its closest textual parallels and reused segments occur in related sections of the *Paṭṭhāna* treating root clusters (*hetu*) and triads, including *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1), *Kusalattika, Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 4.2), *Hetugocchaka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.2), and the immediately preceding *Sahetukadukādi, Kusalattika* (Patthana 21.2) [DharmaNexus]. Further shared passages appear in *Hetusahetukadukādi, Kusalattika* (Patthana 15.25), *Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 2.1), and the primary *Kusalattika* (Patthana 1.2) [DharmaNexus].
